title: Final integration readiness and demonstration preparation
decision_summary: The project is suitable for a carefully qualified research demonstration based on offline code, API, report, and component-rendering evidence. No release-blocking correctness defect was established. Actual local service startup and browser-visible interaction were not verified in this assessment; those remain manual demonstration checks. The outputs are not operationally validated collision-risk or maneuver products.

findings.evidence: README documents Vite at 127.0.0.1:5173 and FastAPI at 127.0.0.1:8000. vite.config.js binds Vite and preview to those loopback addresses. src/api/ssaClient.js defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8000 and honors VITE_API_BASE. Backend import check passed. Frontend API-base tests cover the default and override.
findings.recommended_action: Use the documented local startup commands and confirm both service health and the active catalog source before presenting. Service startup itself was not run under this assessment's no-live-services constraint.

findings.evidence: README previously listed GET /api/conjunctions/{event_id}/maneuver, while backend implements a job-bound POST requiring screening_job_id. README API list was corrected to show POST /api/conjunction-jobs, GET job status, job-bound maneuver POST, Pc input POSTs, and job-bound PDFs. Route signatures were checked against backend/app/main.py.
findings.recommended_action: Use the corrected API route list when manually diagnosing the demonstration.

findings.area: Collision Analysis and Maneuver Assessment integration
findings.evidence: Existing Node and Python regression suites cover accepted job/event binding, physical-event-only selection, proxies that cannot substitute for physical events, missing/cross-job events, stale response suppression, and client verification of response event/job IDs. Backend resolves authoritative stored event states from the requested job. Phase 12.8 report records 83 backend and 65 frontend focused tests; this assessment reran those backend suites and an expanded frontend selection suite.
findings.recommended_action: Keep the selected event ID and accepted screening job ID visible during the live demonstration; do not select a proxy for maneuver assessment.

findings.evidence: Frontend lifecycle/component tests and backend mocked lifecycle tests distinguish complete, partial, failed, running, and valid-empty outcomes. A valid event from a partial job is explicitly marked as partial with incomplete-coverage context. A later failed attempt is kept separate from the prior accepted result.
findings.recommended_action: State the coverage and status displayed for the selected accepted job; do not describe partial coverage as a complete catalog screen.

findings.evidence: Existing regression tests assert warning-qualified available_with_warning results, zero-burn two-body baseline fields, discrepancy labels, event/job association, and unavailable Pc comparison. The UI says candidate miss change is relative to a simulated zero-burn two-body baseline and explicitly says post-maneuver Pc is not calculated.
findings.recommended_action: Describe the output only as an exploratory two-body candidate sweep. Do not claim maneuver effectiveness, risk reduction, or operational safety.

findings.evidence: Backend Pc/CDM tests cover covariance shape/validity, frame, epoch, units, HBR, explicit independence assumptions, event identity, and input failures. Phase 12.7 regression prevents mismatched TCA state metadata/geometry from producing scenario Pc. UI/report regressions keep source-reported Pc and synthetic scenario Pc separate and suppress unavailable, invalid, or out-of-range values instead of converting them to zero.
findings.recommended_action: Explain that TLE-only events lack covariance and measured HBR, so ordinary source Pc is unavailable. Label any scenario Pc as user-assumed sensitivity output, not observed collision probability.

findings.evidence: Job-bound report API tests verify the event and maneuver data come from the requested job. Phase 12.8 added screening_job_id to maneuver responses and PDFs; regression tests verify the report event key/job ID. CSV export metadata includes screening_job_id.
findings.recommended_action: Use job-bound report routes for physical events and confirm report event/job identifiers match the selection.

findings.evidence: Current labels/docs call catalog scores heuristic indices, describe the anomaly score as historical feature unusualness rather than danger/collision risk, and label the exponentiated ESA output as an uncalibrated ESA-scale event-risk estimate rather than Pc. The model card reports the fixed threshold flags 0/55 legacy high-risk test events and states no corrected-protocol model has been validated. Anomaly metadata says no labelled anomaly ground truth exists.
findings.recommended_action: Present these outputs as experimental research context only. Do not call them validated collision-risk classifiers, probabilities of collision, or operational alerts. No inference was run for this assessment.

findings.evidence: Phase 12.9 and current computer-use inventory report no available browser or tabs. No Playwright, Puppeteer, Cypress, or Selenium dependency is installed. Component rendering/API tests are substitutes, not browser interaction. Running the documented Vite/FastAPI services was prohibited, so no interactive application session was started.
findings.recommended_action: Before the presentation, manually start the documented local services and verify one selected physical event, job ID, partial/failed status presentation if applicable, maneuver warning state, unavailable Pc labels, and the event/job IDs in a downloaded report. Record this as a manual smoke check; do not treat it as scientific validation.

findings.evidence: Phase 12.5 provides five deterministic stored TLE encounter fixtures with recorded inputs and repeatability checks. Runtime TleProvider requests CelesTrak groups and can fall back to a bundled TLE sample; live catalog contents and current screening event lists can change with source data and request time. No live feed or job was exercised here.
findings.recommended_action: For repeatable results, present the recorded offline fixture evidence or document the actual source, retrieval time, job ID, horizon, and threshold for a live run. Do not imply the five-case convenience sample is representative.

verified_demonstration_capabilities: The frontend API base and documented local service addresses align; frontend tests cover API base default and override, and backend module import succeeds.
Physical event and screening job identities are bound through the maneuver request/response and job-bound report workflows in focused tests.
Heuristic proxy records remain separate from physical events and cannot be used as maneuver inputs in tested selection/API paths.
Partial, failed, valid-empty, and accepted results have distinct tested statuses; partial coverage and later failed attempts remain distinguishable in tested markup/state.
Source Pc, scenario Pc, unavailable inputs, provenance, warnings, and reason codes remain separate in tested component/report paths; unavailable Pc is not substituted with zero.
Warning-qualified maneuver results and simulated zero-burn comparisons preserve limitations; no post-maneuver Pc result is claimed.
Selected event/job identifiers are retained in tested PDF/CSV paths.
presentation_limitations_to_disclose: Browser-visible layout, navigation, interactions, and actual file download were not verified in this environment.
Actual local application startup and end-to-end service connectivity were not tested; only configuration inspection, backend import, build, and mocked/offline tests were run.
Live TLE data are time-dependent; the provider may use a bundled fallback when live retrieval is unavailable. Record the source status and retrieval metadata shown for the demo.
Normal TLE-only events lack the covariance and measured hard-body radius required for source Pc; missing Pc is unavailable, not zero.
Research scenario Pc depends on user-entered assumptions and is not an observed collision probability.
Maneuver assessment is a warning-qualified exploratory two-body simulation; it does not calculate post-maneuver Pc or establish effectiveness, collision-risk reduction, or operational safety.
Partial screening has incomplete coverage and a small selected fixture set is not representative of the catalog.

Heuristic ranking, anomaly unusualness, and ESA historical log-risk estimation are distinct research outputs, not validated collision-risk classifications; ESA log-risk is not Foster Pc and is not calibrated for operational alerts.
